messages:
maria-support: heads-up — customer jbarker reporting a sudden p95 / p99 latency spike after we pushed the bpe-merge-v2 tokenizer to the new model variant. they say it started ~30m after the rollout and affects long-context requests (>8k tokens).

jbarker-customer: seeing 2.2s -> 8.9s p95 on streaming generate. p99 occasionally hits 15s. same API call as before, no change in prompt.

sophie-oncall: pinging @alex-eng-runtime and @devon-ml — can you triage? customer provided a sample request.

maria-support: sample (redacted keys) from customer:```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"openlab/bison-2.4-redwood","tokenizer":"bpe-merge-v2","input":"<8k-token chat history>...","max_tokens":1024,"stream":true}'```they said they did not change max_tokens.

alex-eng-runtime: looking at infra traces now. early findings: increase in avg tokens-per-request for that prompt family (~1.35x) after tokenizer swap. that alone increases decode work but doesn't fully explain p99 spikes. grabbing flamegraphs and kernel selection logs.

devon-ml: I ran the tokenizer locally against the customer's corpus. bpe-merge-v2 merges differently — in some legal/legalese cases it splits so there are more tokens, in others it merges fewer causing more long tail tokens. net effect: token count variance up, and for some inputs we see +40% tokens.

alex-eng-runtime: also seeing that for sequences >6k tokens we fall back to a different attention kernel (fallback path) because of an unexpected stride in kv cache alignment. fallback kernels are ~3-4x slower on current hw. stack: kernel_selector -> quant_fallback -> attention_fallback.

maria-support: customer wants a workaround ASAP. they asked if pinning to previous tokenizer variant helps.

devon-ml: short term: yes. pin tokenizer to bpe-merge-v1 or force the model variant that uses the old tokenizer mapping. Longer term we should: 1) add tokenization regression tests for high-var token families, 2) fix kv cache alignment in runtime, 3) ensure new tokenizer has a mapping/compat mode.

alex-eng-runtime: mitigation plan I'm pushing now:
- rollback routing for that model tag for enterprise orgs (jbarker's org) to the previous model variant (v1) — immediate.
- add a temporary automatic tokenizer-compatibility toggle in routing to prefer v1 for requests with >6k input tokens.
- emergency patch: short-circuit the fallback kernel by normalizing kv alignment when sequence_len%block_size != 0 — low risk but will need careful perf testing.

deploy-bot: deploy triggered: rollback/model-route (openlab/bison-2.4-redwood -> v1-tokenizer) started by alex-eng-runtime at 2026-03-15T13:20:12Z. CI checks ok.

maria-support: customer confirmed they were routed back to v1 — they reported p95 dropped back to 2.3s within 5 minutes. :thumbsup:

jbarker-customer: thanks team, huge relief. if you can share a repro script we can run to validate on our side, that would be great.

devon-ml: repro steps for engineering and for customer:```# repeatable repro (redwood hosted)
# 1) craft long context ~9k tokens (we used their disabled PII sample)
# 2) call the generate endpoint with tokenizer bpe-merge-v2
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model":"openlab/bison-2.4-redwood",
    "tokenizer":"bpe-merge-v2",
    "input":"<long-context-9k>",
    "max_tokens":512,
    "stream":false
  }' | jq -r '.metrics'```
Look for `tokens_in` and `decode_time_ms`. Compare vs same payload with "tokenizer":"bpe-merge-v1".

alex-eng-runtime: added tracing snippet for us: set header `X-Trace-Mode: full` and we'll capture kernel decisions. sample perf log (trimmed):```[2026-03-15T12:48:01Z] tokens_in=9124 decode_ms=872 kv_alignment=15 fallback_kernel=true kernel_reason=unaligned_stride```

maria-support: action items summary: @alex-eng-runtime rollback done and confirmed; @devon-ml add tokenizer regression tests & a small corpus scan to detect high token variance; @sophie-oncall coordinate a follow-up with customer and schedule postmortem.

devon-ml: I'll open a PR with a corpus test harness for tokenizer variants and add CI gate to prevent future swaps without a tokens-per-request delta check.

alex-eng-runtime: I'll prepare the emergency patch for kv normalization and a perf benchmark. will ship as canary to staging first.

sophie-oncall: assigning a 1-hour postmortem meeting at 1600 UTC to go through root cause, RCA owner @devon-ml.

maria-support: customer wants notes about why this happened so they can explain internally. I'll draft a short incident note once we have the RCA.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started: kv-align-normalize v0.1 -> staging at 2026-03-15T14:05:00Z.

alex-eng-runtime: preliminary root cause (short): tokenizer swap increased tokens-per-request variance for a subset of prompts; for very long contexts that pushed requests into an untested execution path where kv cache alignment was off, triggering a slow fallback kernel. combined effect caused p95/p99 spikes.

maria-support: good. keeping thread open until postmortem posted. thanks all.
